questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly defines a combinational logic circuit as given in the textbook?
options: Combinational Logic Circuits are memoryless digital logic circuits whose output depends on the sequence of past inputs.
Combinational Logic Circuits are memoryless digital logic circuits whose output at any instant in time depends only on the combination of its inputs.
Combinational Logic Circuits are digital circuits that store previous input states to determine their output.
Combinational Logic Circuits are digital logic circuits whose output at any instant depends on both current inputs and internal state.
questions.correctAnswer: Combinational Logic Circuits are memoryless digital logic circuits whose output at any instant in time depends only on the combination of its inputs.
questions.explanation: The textbook definition states that combinational logic circuits are memoryless digital logic circuits whose output at any instant depends only on the combination of its inputs. The other options introduce memory or dependence on past inputs, which are characteristics of sequential circuits, not combinational ones.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes combinational and sequential circuits with respect to memory and feedback?
options: Combinational circuits have no memory and no feedback; sequential circuits have memory and use feedback
Combinational circuits use feedback while sequential circuits do not have memory
Both combinational and sequential circuits use feedback, but only sequential circuits have memory
Combinational circuits have memory but no feedback; sequential circuits have no memory and use feedback
questions.correctAnswer: Combinational circuits have no memory and no feedback; sequential circuits have memory and use feedback
questions.explanation: Combinational circuits produce outputs solely from current inputs, so they contain no storage elements (no memory) and do not employ feedback loops. Sequential circuits include storage elements (e.g., flip‑flops) that provide memory and typically use feedback to retain state across clock cycles.

questions.questionText: Consider a combinational logic circuit where the output Y = A AND B. Initially A=0 and B=1, so Y=0. If the input A changes instantly to 1 while B stays at 1, what will be the new value of Y?
questions.explanation: For an AND gate, Y = A·B. After the change, A=1 and B=1, so Y=1. Because the circuit is combinational, the output reflects the new input values immediately.
